rulings.decided_by: Deletion test (`michael-the-architect` rules); `D7`/`D9` (`TAIKNR_SIDE_STORE_TYPE = "taiknr-side-store"` and `readArchiveBatchesFromBranch(entries): ArchivedToolOutput[][]` in `src/infra/adapters/pi-archive-adapter.ts:5,25-28,53`); `specs/archive-stubbing/spec.md` and `specs/branch-hydration/spec.md` ('Data of the wrong shape').
rulings.answer: Keep the bare non-empty `ArchivedToolOutput[]` array as the `taiknr-side-store` `CustomEntry.data` payload (no `{ v: 1, items }` wrapper). Define a well-formed item once in the design and both spec deltas as a plain object (`typeof x === "object" && x !== null && !Array.isArray(x)`) with `id` (non-empty `string`), `toolName` (`string`), `argsSummary` (`string`), `isError` (`boolean`), `stub` (`string`), and `rawText` (`string`), tolerating extra unknown properties so future additive fields (such as timestamps for the archive-caps card) remain forward- and backward-compatible. Any future breaking change uses a new `customType` rather than sniffing an envelope. On hydration (`readArchiveBatchesFromBranch`), validate per entry: skip any `CustomEntry` whose `customType !== TAIKNR_SIDE_STORE_TYPE`, whose `data` is not a non-empty array, or where any element fails the item guard. Fold valid batches in `getBranch()` order (root to leaf) through `InMemoryArchiveStore.replaceAll`, so when two entries carry the same `id`, the last well-formed entry on the branch wins.
rulings.dispute: Readiness Owner Question 1 + R3, CR-10, CS-1, CB-4, C5, CS-8: Whether `taiknr-side-store` `CustomEntry.data` should wrap batches in a versioned `{ v: 1, items }` envelope (R3) or stay a bare `ArchivedToolOutput[]` array (proposal/spec, CR-10), plus the exact well-formed item contract, extra-field tolerance, whole-entry vs per-item skipping, and duplicate-id winner.
rulings.evidence: Checked `src/infra/adapters/pi-archive-adapter.ts:5,21-28,53`, `src/domain/archived-output.ts:10-17`, and Pi 1.5.2 `dist/core/session-manager.js:187,1074-1084`: `CustomEntry` is non-LLM internal extension state; `Array.isArray(entry.data)` already identifies v1, tolerating unknown object properties covers additive schema evolution without breaking older readers, and an incompatible future schema would be skipped by v1 readers under either `{ v: 2 }` or a bumped `customType`, so `{ v: 1, items }` fails the deletion test. `InMemoryArchiveStore.replaceAll` calls `Map.set` in iteration order over `getBranch()` (root -> leaf), yielding deterministic branch-last-wins with zero extra dedupe code.

rulings.evidence: Verified in Pi 1.5.2 `dist/core/agent-session.js:635-657,3477-3515` and `dist/core/session-manager.js:974-1007`: in a settled run the tree chain is `toolResult(X) -> assistant(final) -> settlement entries`. Under `CR-1`, `X` remains in `pendingOutputs` after Run 1 settles; if the user then `/tree`-branches from `assistant(final)` (preceding `context_edit(X)`), `toolResult(X)` is still on `getBranch()` with no `context_edit`, so `CR-1` wrongly re-stubs `toolResult(X)` on the new branch (breaking 'The original output is still there') and retains `pendingOutputs` + `originalContentByEntryId` images indefinitely after the final run of a session. Conversely, `_applyBoundaryDrafts` appends in list order, confirming `R2`/`CR-1` that putting `taiknr-side-store` before `context_edit`s eliminates the stubbed-without-archive partial-persist failure mode.
rulings.decided_by: Pi 1.5.2 runtime mechanics (`dist/core/agent-session.js:635-657,3477` and `dist/core/extensions/runner.js:798-813`); `specs/archive-stubbing/spec.md` scenario 'The original output is still there'; `D7` (`src/use-cases/commit-archived-batch.ts:5-6` contract 'Drain pending archived outputs into the ArchiveStore'). Narrow refinement of `S3` fixing draft order (`taiknr-side-store` before `context_edit`s).
rulings.dispute: CR-1 vs R2, C2, CS-7, CR-6: Critic (CR-1) proposes keeping items in `pendingOutputs` until a `context_edit` appears on `getBranch()` so a boundary discarded due to another extension retries on the next settle; Readiness (R2), Structural (CS-7), and Comprehension (C2) keep drain-at-settle, require building drafts before mutating state, place the `taiknr-side-store` custom draft before `context_edit` drafts, and document optimistic cache reconciliation on hydration.
rulings.answer: Reject `CR-1`'s proposal to retain items in `pendingOutputs` across runs until `getBranch()` shows a `context_edit`; keep drain-at-settlement via `commitArchivedBatch`, with `R2`'s safe ordering and draft order: (1) prune ineligible items from `pendingOutputs` in place (deleting their `originalContentByEntryId` keys); (2) if `pendingOutputs` is empty, return `undefined`; (3) call `toSettlementDrafts` BEFORE mutating `store` or draining `pendingOutputs` so an unexpected throw leaves state untouched, and order taiknr's drafts with `{ type: "custom", customType: TAIKNR_SIDE_STORE_TYPE, data: batch }` FIRST followed by the `context_edit` drafts (all appended after `...event.entries`); (4) drain `pendingOutputs` in place into `store` via `commitArchivedBatch` and delete committed IDs from `originalContentByEntryId`; (5) state explicitly in `design.md` and `specs/archive-stubbing/spec.md` (closing `C2` and `CS-7`) that because Pi validates and commits boundary drafts after all handlers return with no post-commit callback, `InMemoryArchiveStore` is an optimistic cache over the branch that reconciles via `replaceAll` on the next hydration event (`session_tree`, `session_compact`, `session_start`), while `taiknr-side-store`-first ordering prevents a partial persist from ever leaving a stub without its raw archive record.

rulings.dispute: C1, CR-2, R4, CS-3: Which source defines active-branch membership (`ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()` vs `event.context.contextEntries`), how to fix the uncheckable 'Pi's recovery omission' author wording, and whether only `replacement: null` edits (CS-3) or any prior `context_edit` null or non-null on `getBranch()` or in `event.entries` (CR-2, C1, R4) disqualifies a pending item.
rulings.answer: Pin the settlement eligibility filter in `agent-before-settle.ts` and `specs/archive-stubbing/spec.md` to two checkable conditions against `ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()` and `event.entries` (never compaction-bounded `event.context.contextEntries`): a pending item with `id` is committable iff (1) `getBranch()` contains a `message` entry with `entry.id === id` and `entry.message.role === "toolResult"`, AND (2) neither `getBranch()` nor `event.entries` already contains any `context_edit` targeting `id` (`targetId === id`, whether `replacement` is `null` or non-null). Reword the spec requirement to state this author-independent rule, keeping Pi recovery omission (`replacement: null`) and a prior extension's `context_edit` (such as redaction) as scenarios under it.
rulings.evidence: Checked `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/session-manager.d.ts:119` (`ContextEditEntry` has `{ type, id, parentId, timestamp, targetId, replacement }` and no author field) and `session-manager.js:201-229,264`: `event.context.contextEntries` omits entries prior to `compaction.firstKeptEntryId` (which would wrongly drop pre-compaction carried-forward items against Q2 -> (a)), while `getBranch()` retains the whole branch. Dropping on any existing `context_edit` targeting `id` in `getBranch()` or `event.entries` uses a simple `Set<string>` of `targetId`s, closes both null-resurrection (Trap 4, CS-3) and overwriting/leaking over an earlier extension's redaction or summary edit (C1, CR-2), and enforces 'Nothing commits twice' structurally.
rulings.decided_by: Joel's Orientation Q1 -> (a) and Q2 -> (a) rulings; Pi 1.5.2 `dist/core/session-manager.d.ts:119` (`ContextEditEntry` schema) and `dist/core/session-manager.js:201-229,264` (`buildContextEntries` vs `getBranch()`, latest-edit-wins).

rulings.evidence: Verified in `src/infra/pi-event-handlers/turn-end.ts:9,11` (`argsByCallId: ReadonlyMap<string, string>`, `originalContentByEntryId: Map<string, unknown[]>`) and `agent-before-settle.ts:6-11` (has mutable `originalContentByEntryId`, no `argsByCallId`). Widening `ReadonlyMap` to `Map` in `turn-end.ts` would require a `MODIFIED` `extension-packaging` delta while still leaking blocked/aborted calls that never reach `turn_end`, for ~150 KB across a 1,000-tool-call session once `parentToolCallId` nested calls are skipped; meanwhile `originalContentByEntryId` (which can hold multi-MB base64 images) is already mutable in both handlers and can be freed completely on every drop and commit without touching any contract.
rulings.dispute: R1, CS-2, CB-3, CR-8, R7: CB-3 and CR-8 recommend deleting `argsByCallId` keys in `turn_end`, and CS-2 asks for one settlement owner releasing both `originalContentByEntryId` and `argsByCallId` on drop/commit, whereas R1 points out `turn-end.ts` types `argsByCallId` as `ReadonlyMap<string, string>` and `agent-before-settle.ts` does not receive `argsByCallId` under the locked `extension-packaging` signatures.
rulings.answer: Take `R1(a)` with strict `originalContentByEntryId` release and zero signature changes (`Modified Capabilities: None`): (1) in `tool-call.ts`, skip nested calls (`if (event.parentToolCallId !== undefined) return;`) and leave `argsByCallId` entries for top-level session tool calls in place for the session's lifetime, documented with a one-line `shortcut:` comment (each entry is `<= 120` chars plus call ID, fresh per session closure); (2) in `turn-end.ts`, write `originalContentByEntryId.set(id, content)` ONLY for items actually staged by `stageToolOutputs` (never unstaged `< minCharsToArchive` results); (3) in `agent-before-settle.ts`, delete `originalContentByEntryId.delete(id)` on BOTH silent drop and commit in the single settlement pass (`CS-2`, `R7`), pinned by a unit test asserting `originalContentByEntryId.size === 0` after a mixed drop-and-commit settlement.

rulings.evidence: Checked `src/domain/archived-output.ts:1-8` (`ToolOutputCandidate` already includes both `entryId` and `toolCallId`, which `R6` overlooked), `src/infra/adapters/pi-archive-adapter.ts:5-35` (`InMemoryArchiveStore` is 27 lines and `TAIKNR_SIDE_STORE_TYPE` is a 1-line Pi `customType` constant consumed only inside `pi-archive-adapter.ts`), and `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/core/session-manager.d.ts:154` (`ProjectedSessionEntry.sourceEntry` is a public exported type whose `message.toolCallId` and `id` are documented fields, avoiding both undocumented object-reference identity `===` and `toolResultEntryIds` `flatMap` misalignment).

rulings.answer: Keep all production code in the existing modules with zero new files and zero changes to `openspec/specs/extension-packaging/spec.md` (`CS-4` rejected; `O4` settled as no new adapter exports): (1) `InMemoryArchiveStore` and `TAIKNR_SIDE_STORE_TYPE` stay in `src/infra/adapters/pi-archive-adapter.ts`; (2) `toToolOutputCandidates(event, argsByCallId)` resolves each `toolResult`'s `entryId` via `event.context.contextEntries` by matching `sourceEntry.type === "message" && sourceEntry.message.role === "toolResult" && sourceEntry.message.toolCallId === tr.toolCallId` (taking the last match in `contextEntries`, falling back to `event.toolResultEntryIds[i]` only if `event.context?.contextEntries` is absent and `event.toolResultEntryIds.length === event.toolResults.length`); (3) because `ToolOutputCandidate` already carries both `entryId` and `toolCallId`, `turn-end.ts` maps staged `item.id -> candidate.toolCallId -> tr.content` into `originalContentByEntryId` without re-resolving `entryId` or adding an adapter export; (4) the ~4-line `tool_call` summary and ~10-line `agent_before_settle` branch/edit `Set` filter live in their single caller handlers (`tool-call.ts`, `agent-before-settle.ts`), following `configuration-loader` rulings 10 and 18.

C4, CR-5, R5, CS-9, O2: Where the 'no text is never staged' rule lives and how multiple text blocks join — CR-5 puts `rawText.length > 0` in `stageToolOutputs`, R5 duplicates the guard in both `toToolOutputCandidates` and `stageToolOutputs`, CS-9 demands a single eligibility seam rather than splitting across adapter and use case, and C4 shows naive `["", ""].join("\n")` produces a 1-char string that falsely stages at `minCharsToArchive: 0`.
rulings.evidence: Checked `src/domain/archived-output.ts:19-21`, `tests/domain/archived-output.test.ts:1-13`, `src/use-cases/stage-tool-outputs.ts:8-10`, `src/infra/adapters/pi-archive-adapter.ts:37-42`, and `jev-context-poc.ts:14-20`. Returning `""` from text extraction whenever `textBlocks.every((b) => b.text.length === 0)` closes `C4`'s `["", ""]` join bug while keeping `toToolOutputCandidates` free of threshold/policy filtering, and guarding `candidate.rawText.length > 0 && shouldArchive(...)` in `stageToolOutputs` gives eligibility a single canonical seam (`CS-9`) that protects both Pi and non-Pi callers (`CR-5`, `R5`).
rulings.answer: Put staging eligibility in one seam (`stageToolOutputs` in `src/use-cases/stage-tool-outputs.ts`), leave `shouldArchive` untouched, and keep `toToolOutputCandidates` pure DTO translation: (1) in `toToolOutputCandidates`, collect `{ type: "text", text: string }` blocks; if at least one text block has `text.length > 0`, set `rawText = textBlocks.map((b) => b.text).join("\n")` (matching `jev-context-poc.ts:14-20`), otherwise set `rawText = ""` (so image-only `[]`, `[""]`, and `C4`'s multi-empty `["", ""]` all yield `""` rather than `"\n"`); (2) whitespace-only non-empty strings (e.g. `"   "`, `length > 0`) count as text (`text.length > 0`, no `.trim()`); (3) `stageToolOutputs` requires `candidate.rawText.length > 0 && shouldArchive(candidate.rawText.length, input.minCharsToArchive)`, so every caller (`turn_end`, use-case unit tests, future `cli/`/`mcp/` adapters) enforces the no-empty-text rule from one home.
rulings.decided_by: `D6`/ADR 0001 (use-case reuse across future `cli/`/`mcp/` entry points); `D9` and `tests/domain/archived-output.test.ts` (locking `shouldArchive` as `>=`); `specs/archive-stubbing/spec.md` ('A tool result carrying no text is never staged'); one-fact-one-place (`CS-9`, `CR-5`).

rulings.dispute: CR-3, zoom-out, O1: Critic (CR-3) flags UTF-16 surrogate-pair splitting at the 180-char preview and 120-char `argsSummary` cuts plus unescaped `U+2028`/`U+2029`/`U+0085` line separators in `JSON.stringify`; zoom-out requires preserving `rawText` verbatim and normalizing only rendered stub fields.
rulings.answer:
Adopt `CR-3` and `zoom-out`'s preservation rule in `src/domain/archived-output.ts`: (1) keep `candidate.rawText` verbatim in `ArchivedToolOutput.rawText`, and keep `<n>` in `(<n> chars, <m> lines)` equal to `candidate.rawText.length`; (2) split `candidate.rawText` on `/
||
| | |/` so `<m>` is that split array's length and `<preview>` joins its first 3 elements with `" | "` and truncates to at most 180 UTF-16 code units without splitting a surrogate pair (if unit `max - 1` is a high surrogate `0xD800-0xDBFF` paired with a low surrogate at `max`, cut at `max - 1`, then normalize via `.toWellFormed()`); (3) apply one shared domain single-line + surrogate-safe truncation helper (max 120 UTF-16 code units, replacing `/
||
| | |/g` with `" "`) both when `tool-call.ts` summarizes `(JSON.stringify(event.input) ?? "")` (capping `argsByCallId` memory) and inside `buildStub(candidate)` on `candidate.argsSummary` and `candidate.toolName` so `buildStub` guarantees a single-line, well-formed UTF-16 stub for any caller.
rulings.decided_by: `specs/archive-stubbing/spec.md` ('The stub is one line naming the output and previewing it'); Node 26.8.1 runtime measurement; ADR 0002 Consequences (settled `context_edit` stubs are permanent on the branch).
rulings.evidence: Measured in Node 26.8.1 (`node -e`): `JSON.stringify({ a: "x\u2028y\u2029z\u0085w" })` leaves literal `\u2028`, `\u2029`, and `\u0085` unescaped in the output string, and `("a".repeat(179) + "🚀").slice(0, 180).isWellFormed()` evaluates to `false` (lone high surrogate `\uD83D`). Placing one pure single-line/code-point-safe helper in `src/domain/archived-output.ts` (outside `extension-packaging`'s locked handler/adapter/port list) avoids duplicating truncation rules while keeping `rawText` untouched.
